note: DTN Content Services cash-bids-table-widget. Read from ONE call to https://api.dtn.com/markets/sites/e0067101/cash-bids?units=us — the site id e0067101 carries this location and its neighbours together, so every one of them is a source file and none of them is new code. IT IS READ THROUGH A BROWSER AND NOT BY A FETCH: DTN answered a server-side probe with "The api key is valid, but it is valid to be used within a browser only", so their gateway scopes these widget keys to browser use. poll.mjs loads https://www.allied.coop/grain/cash-bids in a real Chromium and reads the response their own widget asks for, which means we hold no key at all — theirs is public in their page, as it must be for the widget to work. THE LOCATION KEY IS THE NUMERIC location.id (5389) AND NOT THE NAME: a display name is exactly the thing a vendor re-cases, and some of these names are companies rather than towns. cashRounding is absent because no single rule explained every testable row on this board. The identity guard stays exact. COORDINATES ARE NULL AND THAT IS DELIBERATE: the feed carries no coordinate, and a town centroid is a different place from a yard — measured at 1.4 miles on babgrain-auburn. Geocode the street address before relying on a map pin. Built by scripts/dtn-build.mjs from a dtn-probe log; 6 row(s) for this location. COORDINATES came from geocodes/basis1st-list-2026-08-20.tsv, matched on operator AND town (Allied Cooperative / MAUSTON) — never on town alone, which pairs Ag-Land FS's Elmwood in Illinois with Alcivia's Elmwood in Wisconsin. That file's kept population was sampled against the Census geocoder and ArcGIS at a median of 123 m, with Allied's Hixton at 37 m. It is EVIDENCE AND NOT A FACT — README rule 1 — so check this pin against the operator's own published address before enabling. STATE AND ADDRESS READ, NOT INFERRED. Premier, Allied, Country Partners, Country Visions and Ag-Land FS each publish their own locations list; the state and street below were read off it on 2026-08-25 and not inferred from the operator's headquarters. TURNED BACK OFF AFTER THE FIRST LIVE RUN, and the reason is written here so nobody re-enables it hopefully. It was refused by the cash - basis = futures identity check. That check is not fussiness: it is what catches a board read half-way through an update, and a wrong cash price is the one thing this whole project refuses to publish. 84 rows: floor explains 60, round 64, ceiling 24. None of the three explains the board. Corn futures trade in quarter cents, so a board displaying cash and basis to the whole cent cannot reconstruct the identity exactly and a residual up to 0.75c is structural rather than a torn read. cashRoundingCents exists for exactly that and would make this pass TODAY -- it is deliberately NOT being used here, because widening the tolerance to three ticks also blinds the torn-read guard for this source, and 'the check went green' is not the same as 'the number is right'. What settles it is one more measurement: capture this operator's raw payload and compare the DISPLAYED cash and basis against the unrounded values in it. Ag-Land and CHS were settled that way in an afternoon -- floor-to-the-cent explained 80 of 80 and 12 of 12, and no tolerance was needed.
publicNote: Their publicly posted cash board, read from the feed their own website reads. Cash and basis are their own commercial numbers. The futures quote is carried only so a consumer can re-check cash minus basis; it is not redistributed as a price feed.
